title: Capital improvements vs. repairs and maintenance: why they matter
summary: A capital improvement is a permanent change to a building or other asset that adds value, extends its useful life, or adapts it to a new use, such as replacing a roof, adding a new wing, or installing a new HVAC system. Unlike repairs and maintenance, which keep an asset in its current working condition and are generally deducted in the year they’re paid, capital improvements are capitalized and depreciated over time.
